alternate_names: Sri Venu Gopala Swamy Devasthanam, Nellore

history.period: 1883 (construction recorded by the Nellore district government; no information on any earlier structure)
history.summary: CSV town refinement: the temple is in Moolapet (Mulapet), a locality within Nellore city itself, on Trunk Road — not a separate town. One of Nellore's older city temples, Sri Venugopala Swamy Temple at Moolapet was built in 1883 by Sheshul Ghantabattula Papi Reddy, according to the Nellore district government; the exact earlier history is unrecorded. The south-facing temple has a spacious courtyard, a flagpole with a worn and now-unreadable Telugu construction inscription, Garuda sannidhi, Dashavatara figures above the mandapam and Krishna-leela paintings along the pradakshina path; in the sanctum Venugopala is flanked by Lakshmi and Goda Devi (Andal). The well-known Moolasthaneswara Swamy temple of Moolapet is very close by, there is a separate Narasimha shrine and a newly built Ashtalakshmi temple opposite the main entrance, and a pushkarani (temple tank) outside the courtyard on the east side.

name: Sri Venugopala Swamy Temple, Moolapet
town_description: Moolapet (Mulapet) is an old neighbourhood of Nellore city in Andhra Pradesh, centred on Trunk Road near the city core. It is a temple locality — home to this Venugopala Swamy temple and the nearby famous Moolasthaneswara Swamy temple — within easy reach of Nellore's railway station and bus stands.

travel.airport: Tirupati International Airport, approx. 130 km; taxis and buses to Nellore.
travel.railway: Nellore Junction, approx. 2-3 km from Moolapet, well connected across India.
travel.road: On Trunk Road in central Nellore; city buses, autos and taxis readily available.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Krishnashtami, Vaikuntha Ekadashi and Brahmotsavam periods are the most festive.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Approx. 9:30 AM to 6:30 PM Mon-Sat per Justdial, but another listing reports 9:30 AM to 8:30 PM daily — verify before visiting. Entry is free.
